properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 28 at 11:24AM PDT until October 28 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Rough bar conditions expected during very strong ebb
currents. Seas peaking near 10 ft and west winds 10 to 15 kt
during the very strong ebb current Wednesday evening. Seas
peaking near 8 ft and south winds 10 to 15 kt during the very
strong ebb current Thursday evening.

* WHERE...In the Main Channel of the Columbia River Bar.

* WHEN...Small Craft Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 9 PM
PDT this evening. Small Craft Advisory, from 5 PM to 10 PM PDT
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft,
especially when operating near to, or attempting to cross, the
Columbia River Bar.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very strong ebb current of 6.88 kt at 644
PM Wednesday. Seas 10 ft. Ebb current of 3.43 kt at 720 AM
Thursday. Seas 6 ft. Very strong ebb current of 6.5 kt at 732 PM
Thursday. Seas 8 ft.
properties.instruction:
A Small Craft Advisory means that wave conditions are expected to
be hazardous to small craft in the vicinity of the Columbia River
Bar. Mariners are advised to obtain the latest bar conditions
from the United States Coast Guard before attempting to cross the
bar.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Visibility down to a quarter mile or less in dense fog.

* WHERE...Lower Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM AKDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to low visibility. Near
to below freezing temperatures may lead to frost on bridges and
roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of dense fog will persist across
portions of the Matanuska Valley, especially those locations close
to Knik Arm and the Palmer Airport, through around noon before
quickly diminishing.

less than one quarter mile. If driving, slow down, use your
headlights, and leave plenty of distance ahead of you.

properties.areaDesc: Rio Arriba, NM; Taos, NM
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 28 at 11:51AM MDT until October 30 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Grande at Embudo affecting Rio Arriba and Taos Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Embudo.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Minor overbank flows are occurring above the
Embudo gaging site. Access to riverside picnic facilities above
Pilar and below the Taos Junction Bridge along State Route 570 will
be limited if further rises occur. Water may be extremely close to
underside of bridge over Rio Grande on Aguas Caliente Rd in Pilar.
Other localized effects due to the high water levels will begin to
be felt at a stage of 10 feet but no significant flooding is
expected until the river rises to 12 feet.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday the stage was 7.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.1 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon MDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL FRIDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Rio Arriba, NM
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 11:45AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday was 6.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain between 6.4 and 6.7
feet through the next several days.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.7
feet on 07/21/2009.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon MDT.

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents. There is also a strong north to
south longshore current.

* WHERE...In North Carolina, Coastal New Hanover County. In
South Carolina, Coastal Georgetown County.

* WHEN...Today.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 28 at 10:04AM PDT until October 28 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in
low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near
shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.0 and 9.3 feet MLLW
at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...From noon to 3 PM PDT Wednesday. High tide is at 1:13
PM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater
inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high
tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.
